survey: A refractor telescope on a tripod, standing on grey lunar ground and seen from the front-left at three-quarter view. The cream tube runs diagonally. A wider dew-shield section with a dark blue objective lens sits at the upper right, facing up and away. At the lower left end are a gold ring, a short grey focuser and a rounded grey eyepiece. The tube rests in a grey fork mount: a bracket plate on each side, a pivot bolt on the near plate, and a curved strap that clamps over the top of the tube. The fork is bolted onto a round wooden head plate. Under that plate a gold collar holds three wooden legs: front-left, back-left (partly behind) and right. Each leg ends in a grey rubber foot that touches the ground, with matching contact shadows. The tripod spreads wide enough to stand. The mount sits about a third of the way along the tube, which is believable for a clamped tilt mount. Every part connects to the next: tube to clamp, clamp to fork, fork to head plate, head plate to legs, legs to ground. There are no loose parts, nothing floats, and the leg count is correct.
